key_insight: Multiple disciplines are converging on a unified concept of "Physical AI": systems that are not only predictive or simulated, but embodied, materially grounded, and able to act robustly in the physical world.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between simulation/cognition-focused AI and real-world action by proposing a unified framework and research agenda for designing, evaluating, and deploying physically interacting intelligent systems.
method: Synthesize concepts from robotics, machine learning, neuroscience and materials science to define core principles of Physical AI.
Outline integrated design directions that couple perception, control/learning, morphology/materials and energy constraints in closed physical loops.
Advocate new metrics, benchmarks and experimental platforms to measure real-world performance and robustness beyond simulated tasks.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a practical roadmap to develop agents that generalize and operate safely in the real world, shifting research focus from purely simulated benchmarks to physically grounded evaluation and design.
visual_elements: Continuum diagram showing progression from predictive/simulative AI → embodied intelligence → Physical AI
Layered architecture graphic: sensors/perception → learning/control → morphology/materials → energy/power

Bar/radar chart comparing typical simulation metrics vs. proposed physical-world performance metrics (robustness, adaptation, energy efficiency)
paper_title: From embodied intelligence to physical AI
